translation: adj. 强制的
definitionEn: able to be made effective or obeyed, especially by law

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 可（依法）强制执行的，可强制实现的（法律语境核心义）
uncommonMeanings.example: Without a signature, the deal is not enforceable. 没有签名，这笔交易不具强制力。

posExamples.sentence: The written agreement is legally enforceable.
Clear deadlines make the rule enforceable.
The promise was morally important but not enforceable.

wordForms.noun: enforcement 执行，实施；enforceability 可执行性
wordForms.verb: enforce vt. 强制执行，实施（法律等）
wordForms.adjective: enforceable 可强制执行的；unenforceable 不可强制执行的（前缀 un- 表否定）
wordForms.other: 构词：动词 enforce + -able（可…的）→ 形容词 enforceable；反义前缀 un- → unenforceable。重音在第二音节 en-FOR-ce-a-ble /ɪnˈfɔːsəbl/。同族记忆：force（力量）藏在词根里——「有力可施」即「可强制执行」。

collocations.translation: 可强制执行的合同 / 法律
collocations.example: A verbal promise is rarely an enforceable contract. 口头承诺很少是可强制执行的合同。
The agreement is legally enforceable in court. 该协议在法庭上具法律强制力。

collocations.translation: 可强制实现的权利 / 规则
collocations.example: Citizens should have enforceable rights, not empty words. 公民应享有可强制实现的权利，而非空话。
New penalties make the ban enforceable. 新的处罚使这项禁令得以强制执行。
The lease creates an enforceable obligation. 租约产生了可依法执行的义务。
The order is enforceable against every supplier. 该命令可对每家供应商执行。
These clauses remain enforceable after termination. 这些条款在终止后仍可执行。

collocations.translation: 具有法律约束力且可执行
collocations.example: Both sides signed a binding and enforceable settlement. 双方签署了有约束力且可执行的和解协议。

synonyms.example: The agreement is legally binding on both sides. 该协议对双方均有法律约束力。
synonyms.usage: binding 强调「有约束力、必须遵守」，常作表语（be binding on sb）或定语（a binding contract）；enforceable 强调「可被强制执行、可诉诸法律实现」。二者常连用：a binding and enforceable contract。

synonyms.example: The contract remains valid for one year. 合同一年内有效。
synonyms.usage: valid 侧重「有效、成立」（形式合法），不含「可强制执行」之意；enforceable 侧重「一旦违约可强制落实」。一份合同可能 valid 但因程序缺陷 not enforceable。

advancedExpressions.expression: enforce → enforceable（可执行的）；rely → reliable（可靠的）；avail → available（可用的）；suit → suitable（合适的）
advancedExpressions.example: 动词 + -able 常构成「可被…的」形容词：Rules that cannot be enforced are unenforceable. 无法执行的规则就是不可执行的。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·「有法律效力」
advancedExpressions.expression: legally enforceable = legally binding = have the force of law
advancedExpressions.example: Once signed, the treaty has the force of law and is legally enforceable. 条约一经签署即具法律效力、可强制执行。

advancedExpressions.expression: an enforceable obligation / enforceable against sb / remain enforceable / legally binding and enforceable
advancedExpressions.example: The lease creates an enforceable obligation. 租约产生了可依法执行的义务。

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The written agreement is legally enforceable, so either party can seek a court remedy.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主体、事实与场景，补充结果或后续影响，增强因果层次。

translation: n. 争论，辩论，争端，纠纷 /dɪˈspjuːt/ vi. & vt. 对…提出质询，对…表示异议（或怀疑）；争夺，竞争；争论， 100 辩论，争执
definitionEn: (1) n. a serious disagreement (2) v. to question the truth or validity of something

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 争端，纠纷，争论（重音在第二音节 /dɪˈspjuːt/ 或首音节 /ˈdɪspjuːt/）
uncommonMeanings.example: The pay dispute lasted for weeks. 这场薪资纠纷持续了数周。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 对…提出质疑，对…表示异议（怀疑真实性/正确性）
uncommonMeanings.example: Nobody disputes that he is talented. 没人质疑他有才华。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 争夺，争抢（土地、权力、冠军等）
uncommonMeanings.example: Two teams disputed the championship. 两队争夺冠军。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 争论，争执（dispute with sb about/over sth）
uncommonMeanings.example: They disputed with each other about the plan. 他们就计划相互争执。

posExamples.sentence: Mediators helped settle the border dispute.
The company disputed the final invoice.
Ownership of the painting remains in dispute.

wordForms.noun: dispute 争端，纠纷；disputation 辩论，争论；disputant 争论者
wordForms.verb: dispute vt. & vi. 质疑，争夺，争论
wordForms.adjective: disputable 有争议的，可疑的；indisputable 无可争辩的（前缀 in- 表否定）；disputed 有争议的
wordForms.other: 重音辨析：作名词可读 /ˈdɪspjuːt/（重音前移）或 /dɪˈspjuːt/；作动词重音在后 /dɪˈspjuːt/。近义名词短语提示：settle a dispute ≈ resolve/end a dispute。

idioms.example: Beyond all dispute, he is the best player on the team. 毫无疑问，他是队里最好的球员。
The exact date is still in dispute. 确切日期仍有争议。
Without dispute, she deserved the prize. 她当之无愧地赢得了这个奖。

collocations.translation: 法律 / 土地 / 贸易纠纷
collocations.example: They went to court to settle a land dispute. 他们上法庭解决一起土地纠纷。
The two sides finally settled the dispute peacefully. 双方最终和平解决了纠纷。
There is a dispute over who owns the copyright. 就版权归属存在争端。
The ownership of the land is still in dispute. 这块地的归属仍有争议。
Her talent is beyond dispute. 她的才华无可争辩。

collocations.translation: 对某主张 / 决定提出质疑
collocations.example: He disputed the referee's decision angrily. 他愤怒地对裁判的判罚提出异议。
A customer lodged a dispute over the charge. 一名顾客对该收费提出争议。
The long-running dispute finally reached arbitration. 这场长期争议最终进入仲裁。

synonyms.example: A small argument grew into a serious dispute. 一场小争论演变成严重纠纷。
synonyms.usage: argument 指「（讲道理的）争论、论点」，quarrel 指「（带情绪的）口角争吵」；dispute 更正式，多指「（尤指公共/法律层面）持续的纠纷、争端」，常搭 legal/trade/land dispute。

synonyms.example: The border conflict escalated into war. 边界冲突升级为战争。
synonyms.usage: conflict 语义更重，含「对立、矛盾甚至武力冲突」；dispute 侧重「就具体分歧的争论/纠纷」，可通过谈判 settle。

synonyms.example: He questioned the accuracy of the report. 他质疑报告的准确性。
synonyms.usage: 作动词表「质疑」时，dispute = question/challenge，后接名词或 that 从句：dispute a claim / dispute that…；challenge 更强调「公开挑战、要求对方证明」。

advancedExpressions.expression: settle / resolve / end a dispute（解决）；a dispute over sth（关于…的争端）；in dispute（有争议）；beyond dispute（无可争辩）
advancedExpressions.example: They set up a committee to resolve the trade dispute over tariffs. 他们成立委员会解决关税贸易争端。

advancedExpressions.expression: beyond dispute = without doubt = it is undeniable that…
advancedExpressions.example: It is undeniable that / Beyond dispute, education changes lives. 无可争辩，教育改变命运。

advancedExpressions.expression: beyond dispute / dispute a claim / decision / raise / lodge a dispute / a long-running dispute
advancedExpressions.example: Her talent is beyond dispute. 她的才华无可争辩。

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Mediators helped settle the border dispute, preventing the disagreement from escalating.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主体、事实与场景，补充结果或后续影响，增强因果层次。

classPractice.question: The two families have been in ____ (dispute) over the ownership of the field for years.
classPractice.note: 固定短语 in dispute「有争议的，在争论中」，dispute 在此作名词，前不加冠词。

classPractice.question: 毫无疑问，她是最合格的候选人。____ ____, she is the most qualified candidate.
classPractice.note: 固定表达 beyond dispute「无可争辩地」置于句首作状语。

classPractice.question: It is ____ (dispute) that the Great Wall is a masterpiece of human history. (用否定形容词)
classPractice.note: 原题型标注：词形填空。in- (否定) + disput + -able → indisputable「无可争辩的」，It is indisputable that… 是常用句型。

translation: adj. 游牧的，流浪的
original_sentence: Around 12,000 years ago in the Middle East, small permanent farming communities were established, changing traditional nomadic hunter-gatherer lifestyles.
definitionEn: moving from place to place rather than living permanently in one location

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 游牧的（逐水草而居，居无定所）
uncommonMeanings.example: Nomadic herders follow their sheep across the plains. 游牧民赶着羊群穿越平原。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （比喻）漂泊不定的，四处迁移的（指人生活/工作不固定）
uncommonMeanings.example: As a journalist, she has a rather nomadic career. 作为记者，她的职业相当漂泊不定。

posExamples.sentence: Nomadic herders moved with the changing seasons.
The family maintained a largely nomadic lifestyle.
Some birds have nomadic movement patterns.

wordForms.noun: nomad 游牧者，流浪者；nomadism 游牧生活（方式）
wordForms.adjective: nomadic 游牧的，流浪的
wordForms.other: 构词：名词 nomad + -ic（…的）→ 形容词 nomadic。重音在第二音节 no-MA-dic /nəʊˈmædɪk/。反义联想：settled / sedentary（定居的）↔ nomadic（游牧的）。

collocations.translation: 游牧狩猎采集的生活方式（课文原句）
collocations.example: …changing traditional nomadic hunter-gatherer lifestyles. 改变了传统的游牧狩猎采集生活方式。
They led a nomadic life, moving with the seasons. 他们过着随季节迁徙的游牧生活。

collocations.translation: 游牧部落 / 民族 / 牧民
collocations.example: Nomadic tribes crossed the vast grassland. 游牧部落穿越广袤草原。
For years he lived a nomadic existence with no fixed home. 多年来他过着居无定所的漂泊生活。
The survey included a remote nomadic community. 调查涵盖了一个偏远游牧群体。
The people were traditionally nomadic. 这个族群传统上过游牧生活。
Semi-nomadic families return each winter. 半游牧家庭每年冬天都会返回。
Development blocked several nomadic migration routes. 开发工程阻断了数条游牧迁徙路线。

synonyms.example: A wandering tribe set up camp by the river. 一个流浪部落在河边扎营。
synonyms.usage: wandering/roaming 泛指「漫无目的地四处走动/漂泊」，可修饰人、动物；nomadic 特指「（民族/群体）以放牧为生、逐水草迁徙」的生活方式，更正式、更专指文化形态。

synonyms.example: Migratory birds fly south in winter. 候鸟冬季南飞。
synonyms.usage: migratory 强调「季节性、规律性的迁徙」（多指动物或人口迁移）；nomadic 强调「一种长期无固定居所的生活方式」，二者语义相近但侧重点不同。

advancedExpressions.type: 构词法·-ic 形容词后缀
advancedExpressions.expression: nomad → nomadic；hero → heroic；base → basic；drama → dramatic
advancedExpressions.example: 名词 + -ic 常构成形容词：a nomad（游牧者）→ a nomadic tribe（游牧部落）。

advancedExpressions.expression: lead / live a nomadic (settled / simple / busy) life；a nomadic existence
advancedExpressions.example: After giving up city life, they chose to lead a more nomadic existence. 放弃城市生活后，他们选择过更漂泊的生活。

advancedExpressions.expression: a nomadic community / traditionally nomadic / semi-nomadic / nomadic migration routes
advancedExpressions.example: The survey included a remote nomadic community. 调查涵盖了一个偏远游牧群体。

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Nomadic herders moved with the changing seasons, following fresh pasture across the plateau.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主体、事实与场景，补充结果或后续影响，增强因果层次。

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The family maintained a largely nomadic lifestyle, carrying only what could fit in their vehicle.

classPractice.question: About 12,000 years ago, farming gradually replaced the ____ (nomad) hunter-gatherer way of life.
classPractice.note: 修饰名词 way of life 需用形容词，名词 nomad + -ic → nomadic「游牧的」（对齐课文原句）。

classPractice.question: The desert ____ (游牧者) travel from oasis to oasis in search of water.
classPractice.note: 原题型标注：词形填空。此处作主语需名词 nomad「游牧者」，复数加 -s。形容词 nomadic 不能作主语。

classPractice.note: 原题型标注：汉译英（完成句子）。lead a nomadic life「过游牧生活」，led 为 lead 的过去式；nomadic 作定语修饰 life。

translation: adj. （机器、体系等）复杂巧妙的，先进的，精密的；见多识广的，老练的，见过世面的；水平高的，在行的
original_sentence: Over time, laws evolve to become more sophisticated and wide-ranging.
definitionEn: (1) advanced and complex (2) showing refined knowledge or experience

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （机器、体系、方法等）复杂巧妙的，先进的，精密的（课文义）
uncommonMeanings.example: Modern planes rely on sophisticated computer systems. 现代飞机依赖精密的电脑系统。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （人）见多识广的，老练的，见过世面的
uncommonMeanings.example: He is a sophisticated traveller who speaks five languages. 他是个见过世面、会说五种语言的旅行家。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 水平高的，高雅的，精致的（品味、艺术等）
uncommonMeanings.example: The restaurant offers sophisticated dishes. 这家餐厅供应精致的菜肴。

posExamples.sentence: The laboratory uses sophisticated imaging equipment.
Her argument was sophisticated but easy to follow.
The restaurant attracts a sophisticated audience.

wordForms.noun: sophistication 复杂精密；老练，世故；sophisticate n. 老于世故的人
wordForms.verb: sophisticate vt. 使复杂化；使老练（较少用）
wordForms.adjective: sophisticated 复杂精密的；老练的；unsophisticated 单纯的，不老练的（前缀 un- 表否定）
wordForms.other: 重音在第二音节 so-PHIS-ti-ca-ted /səˈfɪstɪkeɪtɪd/，共五个音节，易读错，注意 -cated 读 /keɪtɪd/。反义联想：simple / naive / crude ↔ sophisticated。

collocations.phrase: laws evolve to become more sophisticated and wide-ranging
collocations.translation: 法律演变得更复杂精密、涵盖面更广（课文原句）
collocations.example: Over time, laws evolve to become more sophisticated and wide-ranging. 随着时间推移，法律演变得更加精密、覆盖面更广。

collocations.translation: 先进精密的技术 / 设备 / 系统
collocations.example: The lab uses highly sophisticated equipment. 该实验室使用高度精密的设备。

collocations.translation: 复杂精巧的方法 / 手段
collocations.example: They developed a sophisticated approach to data analysis. 他们开发了一套精巧的数据分析方法。

collocations.translation: 见多识广（有鉴赏力）的观众 / 读者
collocations.example: The film appeals to a sophisticated audience. 这部影片迎合有鉴赏力的观众。
She has sophisticated tastes in art. 她在艺术上品味高雅。
The attack used highly sophisticated methods. 这次攻击采用了高度复杂的方法。
The device is technically sophisticated but reliable. 该设备技术先进且可靠。
Fraud schemes have become increasingly sophisticated. 诈骗手段变得日益复杂。

synonyms.example: China has developed advanced high-speed rail technology. 中国研发了先进的高铁技术。
synonyms.usage: advanced 强调「（发展阶段上）领先、高级」；sophisticated 强调「（构造/设计上）复杂精密、考虑周全」。修饰技术设备二者常通用：sophisticated/advanced technology。

synonyms.example: The problem is more complex than it looks. 这个问题比看上去更复杂。
synonyms.usage: complex/complicated 是中性「复杂」（可能难懂难处理）；sophisticated 含褒义「复杂而精巧、高明」。说系统「精密先进」用 sophisticated，说系统「繁琐难懂」用 complicated。

synonyms.example: Living abroad made her more worldly. 旅居国外使她更通晓世事。
synonyms.usage: 指「人」时 sophisticated = worldly/experienced「见多识广、老练」；反义 naive/unsophisticated「天真、涉世未深」。此义作表语或定语修饰人：a sophisticated woman。

advancedExpressions.type: 仿写范句·evolve（配套课件仿写句）
advancedExpressions.expression: Over the past three years of high school, I have evolved from a shy teenager who was afraid to speak up into a confident young man willing to take on leadership roles.
advancedExpressions.example: 高中三年，我从一个不敢开口的害羞少年，成长为一个愿意承担领导角色的自信青年。（对应课文 laws evolve to become more sophisticated，仿写聚焦 evolve from…into… 结构）

advancedExpressions.type: 仿写范句·evolve（配套课件仿写句）
advancedExpressions.expression: Over the course of the journey, his understanding of strength evolved — from physical power to quiet, persistent perseverance.
advancedExpressions.example: 在旅途中，他对「力量」的理解逐渐演变——从体魄之力，到静默而坚韧的毅力。（evolve 表「（逐渐）演变、进化」，与 sophisticated 同句拓展）

advancedExpressions.expression: sophisticated ≈ highly advanced ≈ state-of-the-art（最先进的）≈ cutting-edge（尖端的）
advancedExpressions.example: The hospital is equipped with state-of-the-art, sophisticated scanners. 医院配备了最先进、最精密的扫描仪。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The laboratory uses sophisticated imaging equipment.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The laboratory uses sophisticated imaging equipment, revealing structures too small for ordinary cameras.

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Her argument was sophisticated but easy to follow, combining several theories without losing clarity.

classPractice.note: 对齐课文原句，become 后需形容词作表语，动词 sophisticate 的 -ed 形容词形式 sophisticated「复杂精密的」。

classPractice.question: The engineers designed a ____ control system that automatically adjusts to weather changes.
classPractice.note: 原题型标注：辨析选词（sophisticated / complicated）。此处褒义「复杂而精巧、高明」用 sophisticated；若指「繁琐难懂」才用 complicated。

classPractice.question: Years of travel gave the diplomat a certain ____ (sophisticated) that impressed everyone.
classPractice.note: 原题型标注：词形填空。冠词 a certain 后需名词，形容词 sophisticated 的名词形式 sophistication「老练，世故」。

translation: vt. 废除，废止
definitionEn: to officially end a law, system, practice, or institution

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 废除，废止（正式地终止法律、制度、习俗等；对象多为抽象事物）
uncommonMeanings.example: The two houses of parliament voted to abolish the tax. 议会两院投票废除该税。

posExamples.sentence: Parliament voted to abolish the outdated fee.
The reform abolished several discriminatory rules.
Many campaigners sought to abolish child labour.

wordForms.noun: abolition 废除，废止；abolitionist 废奴主义者，废除论者
wordForms.verb: abolish vt. 废除，废止
wordForms.adjective: abolished 被废除的
wordForms.other: 重音在第二音节 a-BO-lish /əˈbɒlɪʃ/。名词后缀突变：abolish → abolition（-ish 变 -ition）。搭配提示：abolish 的宾语多为制度/法律/习俗等抽象名词，不接具体物品（废除具体物用 remove/get rid of）。

collocations.example: Outdated laws are abolished when they no longer correspond with the values of society. 当过时的法律不再符合社会价值观时便被废除。

collocations.translation: 废除一项法律 / 规定 / 制度
collocations.example: The government decided to abolish the outdated rule. 政府决定废除这条过时的规定。
Many countries have abolished the death penalty. 许多国家已废除死刑。
The city abolished parking fees in the old town. 该市取消了老城区的停车费。

collocations.phrase: call for sth to be abolished
collocations.example: Campaigners called for the restriction to be abolished. 活动人士呼吁废除该限制。
The office was formally abolished in 1998. 该机构于1998年正式撤销。
The abolition of the tax benefited small firms. 取消该税使小企业受益。
The policy aims to abolish discrimination in hiring. 该政策旨在消除招聘歧视。

synonyms.example: They cancelled the meeting because of the storm. 因暴风雨他们取消了会议。
synonyms.usage: cancel 指「取消（某次活动、安排、订单）」，对象具体、可临时；abolish 指「（正式、永久地）废除（制度、法律、习俗）」，语气正式、影响长远。二者不可互换。

synonyms.example: We should get rid of this outdated regulation. 我们应废除这条过时的规定。
synonyms.usage: get rid of 口语化，通用「除去（任何讨厌的东西）」；abolish 正式，专用于「废除制度性事物」。写作正式语体优先 abolish。

synonyms.example: The plan aims to eliminate poverty by 2035. 该计划旨在2035年前消除贫困。
synonyms.usage: eliminate 强调「彻底清除（问题、障碍、竞争对手等）」；abolish 专指「以法律/官方手段废止（制度、法律）」。废除法律用 abolish，消除贫困用 eliminate。

advancedExpressions.type: 仿写范句·correspond with（配套课件仿写句）
advancedExpressions.expression: Educational policies must correspond with the evolving needs of society and the aspirations of young people.
advancedExpressions.example: 教育政策必须与社会不断变化的需求和年轻人的抱负相契合。（对应课文 abolished when they no longer correspond with…，仿写聚焦 correspond with「与…相符/相契合」）

advancedExpressions.type: 仿写范句·correspond with（配套课件仿写句）
advancedExpressions.expression: For years, they corresponded with each other across oceans, their letters bridging distance and time.
advancedExpressions.example: 多年来，他们隔着海洋通信，信件跨越了距离与时间。（correspond with 另一义「与…通信」，一词多义拓展）

advancedExpressions.expression: abolish（废除制度法律）≈ do away with（废除，摒弃）≈ put an end to（终止）
advancedExpressions.example: Reformers fought for years to do away with / abolish slavery. 改革者奋斗多年以废除奴隶制。

translation: vt. 修正，修订
definitionEn: to change a law, document, statement, or proposal in order to improve or correct it

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 修正，修订（正式地修改法律、文件、协议中的文字/条款）
uncommonMeanings.example: The report was amended to include new data. 报告经修订加入了新数据。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （amends，复数）赔偿，赔罪，弥补（固定搭配 make amends）
uncommonMeanings.example: She made amends by apologizing sincerely. 她真诚道歉以作弥补。

posExamples.sentence: Lawmakers amended the bill after public consultation.
Please amend the report before publication.
The parties agreed to amend the contract.

wordForms.noun: amendment 修正案，修订；amends（复数）赔偿，弥补
wordForms.verb: amend vt. 修正，修订
wordForms.adjective: amended 修订后的；amendable 可修改的
wordForms.other: 重音在第二音节 a-MEND /əˈmend/。辨形警示：amend（修订）≠ emend（校订文本，罕见）≠ mend（修补东西）。派生名词 amendment 常指宪法/法律的「修正案」，如美国宪法的 the First Amendment。

idioms.example: He sent flowers to make amends for forgetting her birthday. 他送花以弥补忘记她生日之过。

collocations.phrase: amend a law / the constitution / a rule
collocations.translation: 修订法律 / 宪法 / 规则
collocations.example: Parliament voted to amend the constitution. 议会投票修订宪法。

collocations.translation: 修改文件 / 合同 / 方案
collocations.example: Please amend the contract before signing. 签字前请先修改合同。
The rule was amended to protect consumers. 该规则经修订以保护消费者。
He tried to make amends for his mistake. 他努力弥补自己的过错。
They amended the motion by adding a deadline. 他们通过加入截止日期修订了动议。
The guidance was amended to reflect new evidence. 指南经修订以反映新证据。
Voters approved the constitutional amendment. 选民通过了宪法修正案。
He promised to amend his ways after the warning. 他受到警告后承诺改过。

synonyms.example: She revised her essay several times. 她把文章修改了好几遍。
synonyms.usage: revise 通用「修改、订正（文章、计划、观点等）」，语域较宽；amend 更正式，多指「修订法律、宪法、正式文件的具体条款」。改法律用 amend，改作文用 revise。

synonyms.example: They modified the design to cut costs. 他们修改设计以降低成本。
synonyms.usage: modify 强调「（部分地）调整、改动以适应需要」，对象常为设计、行为、计划；amend 侧重「对正式文本的文字性修订」。二者语义相近，法律语境优先 amend。

synonyms.example: Please correct the spelling mistakes. 请改正拼写错误。
synonyms.usage: correct 指「改正（错误）」，重在把错的改对；amend 指「修订、完善（条款内容）」，不一定原文有错。改错误用 correct，完善条款用 amend。

advancedExpressions.expression: amend a law（修订法律）；an amendment to the constitution（宪法修正案）；make amends for sth（弥补过错）
advancedExpressions.example: After the amendment to the traffic law, drivers must make amends for any damage they cause. 交通法修订后，司机须对造成的损失作出赔偿。

advancedExpressions.expression: amend → amendment（修正案）；govern → government；agree → agreement；develop → development
advancedExpressions.example: 动词 + -ment 常构成抽象名词：They proposed an amendment to the bill. 他们对该法案提出一项修正案。

advancedExpressions.expression: amend ≈ make changes to ≈ revise ≈ alter
advancedExpressions.example: The committee decided to amend / make changes to the outdated regulations. 委员会决定修订过时的规定。

translation: n. 霸凌，欺凌
definitionEn: repeated behaviour intended to hurt, frighten, or control someone with less power

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （不可数）霸凌，欺凌（以强凌弱、恐吓的行为）
uncommonMeanings.example: Bullying is not tolerated in our school. 我校绝不容忍霸凌。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 恃强凌弱的，威吓人的（用作定语或分词）
uncommonMeanings.example: His bullying manner frightened the younger kids. 他仗势欺人的样子吓坏了小孩子们。

posExamples.sentence: The school introduced a policy against bullying.
Online bullying can follow children into their homes.
Witnesses should report bullying promptly.

wordForms.noun: bully（恃强凌弱者，恶霸）/ bullying（霸凌行为）
wordForms.verb: bully（vt. 欺凌，恐吓；bully sb into doing 胁迫某人做）
wordForms.other: 构词：bully（名词/动词）+ -ing → 动名词/名词 bullying。辨析 bully-bullied-bullied，重读在第一音节 /ˈbʊli/。常见搭配 bully sb into (doing) sth 胁迫某人做某事。

collocations.example: School bullying can leave lasting scars on a child's mind. 校园霸凌会给孩子的心灵留下长久创伤。
Cyberbullying spreads faster than face-to-face bullying. 网络霸凌比当面欺凌传播得更快。
The new policy aims to put a stop to bullying on campus. 新规旨在制止校园霸凌。
He was a victim of bullying for years. 他多年来一直是霸凌的受害者。
Teachers must report any bullying behaviour at once. 老师必须立即上报任何霸凌行为。
We should teach children to stand up to bullying. 我们应教孩子勇敢反抗霸凌。
Students can report bullying anonymously. 学生可以匿名举报霸凌。
Anti-bullying measures include staff training. 反霸凌措施包括员工培训。

synonyms.example: The company has a zero-tolerance policy on harassment. 公司对骚扰行为零容忍。
synonyms.usage: harassment 侧重反复的骚扰（性骚扰、职场骚扰均可），多为正式/法律用语；bullying 侧重以强凌弱的欺凌，校园语境常用。两者均为不可数名词。

synonyms.example: Witnesses were kept silent through intimidation. 证人因受恐吓而保持沉默。
synonyms.usage: intimidation 强调用威胁使人害怕、屈服，语气更重、更正式；bullying 更口语、更聚焦持续的欺压行为。

synonyms.example: They fought against political oppression. 他们反抗政治压迫。
synonyms.usage: oppression 多指制度性、群体性的长期压迫（政治、社会层面）；bullying 多为个人对个人的欺凌，范围较小。

advancedExpressions.expression: bully sb / pick on sb / push sb around / intimidate sb / harass sb
advancedExpressions.example: Stop picking on your little brother! 别再欺负你弟弟了！（pick on sb = 找茬欺负某人，口语色彩强）

advancedExpressions.expression: put a stop to / crack down on / stand up to / speak out against
advancedExpressions.example: Schools must crack down on bullying and encourage students to speak out. 学校必须严厉打击霸凌并鼓励学生发声。

advancedExpressions.expression: 动词 + -ing 转为表行为的抽象名词：bully→bullying, tease→teasing, cheat→cheating
advancedExpressions.example: Bullying and teasing are both forms of aggression. 霸凌和取笑都是攻击行为的形式。

translation: n. 立法机关
original_sentence: In the civil law system, laws are created by the country’s legislature.
definitionEn: a body of people with the authority to make laws for a country or region

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 立法机关，立法机构（有制定和修改法律权力的机构，如议会、国会）
uncommonMeanings.example: The legislature has the power to make and amend laws. 立法机关有权制定和修订法律。

posExamples.sentence: The legislature approved the environmental bill.
Several teachers were elected to the state legislature.
The proposal returned to the legislature for review.

wordForms.noun: legislature（立法机关）/ legislation（立法，法规[总称，不可数]）/ legislator（立法者，议员）
wordForms.verb: legislate（vi./vt. 立法，制定法律）
wordForms.adjective: legislative（立法的，有立法权的）
wordForms.other: 词根 legis-（法律，源自拉丁 lex/legis）+ -lature。重音在第一音节 /ˈledʒɪslətʃə/。三个易混名词：legislature=机构（谁立的法），legislation=法规本身（不可数），legislator=人（立法者）。行政/司法对照：立法 legislative、行政 executive、司法 judicial。

collocations.translation: 由该国立法机关制定（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: In the civil law system, laws are created by the country's legislature. 在大陆法系中，法律由该国立法机关制定。
The bill was passed by the national legislature. 该法案获国家立法机关通过。

collocations.phrase: pass a law through the legislature
collocations.translation: 使法律通过立法机关（获得通过）
collocations.example: It took two years to pass the reform through the legislature. 这项改革花了两年才在立法机关获得通过。
As a member of the legislature, she voted against the tax. 作为立法机关成员，她投票反对征税。
The state legislature meets twice a year. 州立法机关一年开会两次。
The country has a bicameral legislature. 该国实行两院制立法机关。
A new legislature was elected in spring. 新一届立法机关于春季选出。
The constitution divides legislative authority. 宪法划分了立法权。

synonyms.example: The proposal was debated in parliament. 该提案在议会中被辩论。
synonyms.usage: parliament 特指议会制国家的具体议会机构（如英国 Parliament）；legislature 是泛称，指任何拥有立法权的机构，更学术、更中性。

synonyms.translation: n. 国会（尤指美国国会）
synonyms.example: Congress approved the budget. 国会批准了预算。
synonyms.usage: Congress 特指美国国会（首字母大写为专名）；legislature 为通用抽象名词，可指各国各级立法机构。

synonyms.example: The National Assembly held an emergency session. 国民议会召开了紧急会议。
synonyms.usage: assembly 常用于部分国家立法机构或联合国 General Assembly；legislature 更强调其立法职能本身。

advancedExpressions.expression: legislature（机构）/ legislation（法规，不可数）/ legislator（立法者，人）
advancedExpressions.example: The legislature passed new legislation, and each legislator explained the vote. 立法机关通过了新法规，每位议员都解释了投票理由。

advancedExpressions.expression: the legislative / executive / judicial branch（立法、行政、司法三大分支）
advancedExpressions.example: Power is divided among the legislative, executive and judicial branches. 权力分立于立法、行政、司法三个分支。

advancedExpressions.type: 构词法·-ature 表机构/集合
advancedExpressions.expression: legislate → legislature（立法机关）；类似 judicial → judicature（司法机关）
advancedExpressions.example: The legislature and the judicature perform different roles. 立法机关与司法机关职能不同。

classPractice.note: 第一空指机构（谁通过），用 legislature；第二空指通过的法规（不可数），用 legislation。

translation: adj. 遵纪守法的，安分守己的
original_sentence: The law is the compass that has guided humans from the first law-abiding communities to where we are today.
definitionEn: obeying the law and behaving responsibly within it

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 遵纪守法的，安分守己的（尊重并遵守法律的）
uncommonMeanings.example: A law-abiding society depends on shared respect for rules. 守法的社会依赖对规则的共同尊重。

posExamples.sentence: Law-abiding citizens still need to understand their rights.
The community is peaceful and law-abiding.
A law-abiding business keeps accurate records.

wordForms.noun: law（法律）/ abidance（遵守[较正式，少用]）
wordForms.verb: abide（vi. 遵守[by]；忍受[常用于否定 can't abide]）
wordForms.adjective: law-abiding（遵纪守法的）
wordForms.other: 构词：law（名词）+ abide（动词）的现在分词 abiding，用连字符构成复合形容词 law-abiding，字面即'守法'。同类复合形容词：peace-loving（爱好和平的）、time-consuming（耗时的）、record-breaking（破纪录的）、hard-working（勤奋的）——名词/副词 + 现在分词。动词 abide by = 遵守（规则/决定/承诺）。

collocations.translation: 最初遵纪守法的社群（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: The law is the compass that has guided humans from the first law-abiding communities to where we are today. 法律是指南针，引领人类从最初遵纪守法的社群走到今天。
He has always been a law-abiding citizen. 他一向是守法公民。

collocations.phrase: a law-abiding citizen of high integrity
collocations.translation: 品行端正、遵纪守法的公民（课文延伸）
collocations.example: Observing the law makes you a law-abiding citizen of high integrity. 守法使你成为品行端正的守法公民。
Most residents here are peaceful and law-abiding. 这里多数居民爱好和平、遵纪守法。
The rule confused otherwise law-abiding drivers. 该规则使一向守法的司机困惑。
Education encourages law-abiding behaviour. 教育鼓励守法行为。
Most protesters remained peaceful and law-abiding. 大多数抗议者保持和平守法。
Trust supports a stable, law-abiding society. 信任支撑稳定守法的社会。

synonyms.example: The obedient dog followed every command. 那只听话的狗服从每一道命令。
synonyms.usage: obedient 泛指服从命令/权威（人、动物皆可，to sb）；law-abiding 特指守法（对法律而言），褒义、书面。作定语或表语均可。

synonyms.translation: adj. 顺从的；（尤指）合规的
synonyms.example: The factory is fully compliant with safety rules. 该工厂完全符合安全规定。
synonyms.usage: compliant with sth = 符合（法规/标准），常用于产品/机构合规；law-abiding 更强调人的守法品格，主语多为人或群体。

synonyms.example: She is an upright and honest official. 她是一位正直诚实的官员。

translation: n. 话题，主题；学科，科目；（研究/实验的）对象，受试者；（君主国的）臣民，国民；【语法】主语　adj.（与 to 连用）受…管辖的，须服从的；易受…影响的；以…为条件的　vt. /səbˈdʒekt/ 使遭受，使经受；使服从，征服
sub_section: 补充词汇（课件重点·非词汇表）
definitionEn: the topic, person or thing that is being discussed, studied or dealt with; a branch of knowledge taught at school; (adj., with to) controlled by, likely to be affected by, or dependent on sth; (v.) to make sb/sth undergo or submit to sth, often sth unpleasant

uncommonMeanings.meaning: be subject to sth：受…管辖／须服从…；易受…影响；以…为条件
uncommonMeanings.example: Even senior officials are subject to the law.｜连高级官员也要受法律约束。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: /səbˈdʒekt/ subject sb/sth to sth：使遭受，使经受（常用被动 be subjected to）
uncommonMeanings.example: New drugs are subjected to years of strict testing before they go on sale.｜新药上市前要经受多年的严格检验。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （君主国的）臣民，国民（与共和国的 citizen 相对）
uncommonMeanings.example: Loyal subjects once swore an oath to the king.｜昔日的臣民要向国王宣誓效忠。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （实验或调查的）对象，受试者
uncommonMeanings.example: Ten subjects took part in the memory test.｜十名受试者参加了记忆测试。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【语法】主语
uncommonMeanings.example: In this sentence, 'the court' is the subject.｜在这个句子里，the court 是主语。

posExamples.sentence: Intellectual property is the subject of today's class debate.｜知识产权是今天课堂辩论的主题。
Nobody is above the law; all of us are subject to it.｜没有人凌驾于法律之上，我们都受它约束。
The lab subjected every new design to a strict safety test.｜实验室让每件新设计都经受了严格的安全测试。

collocations.phrase: be subject to the law / to the same rules
collocations.example: Under the constitution, even the president is subject to the law.｜依照宪法，即使总统也受法律约束。

collocations.translation: 可能变动；须经批准（正式告示语）
collocations.example: Patent filing fees are subject to change without notice.｜专利申请费可能调整，恕不另行通知。
Officials subjected every package at the border to a careful check.｜边检人员让每个包裹都经过了仔细检查。

collocations.phrase: the subject of a lawsuit / a patent
collocations.translation: 诉讼的标的；专利所涉之物
collocations.example: That secret formula is now the subject of a patent dispute.｜那个秘方如今成了专利纠纷的标的。
He quickly changed the subject when piracy was mentioned.｜一提到盗版，他就迅速岔开了话题。
On the subject of trademarks, our lawyer gave three warnings.｜关于商标，我们的律师给出了三点提醒。
Basic law has become an elective subject in our school.｜基础法律已成为我校的一门选修课。

collocations.translation: 英国臣民（君主国国民的旧称）
collocations.example: In the days of the empire, anyone born in its territories was a British subject.｜在帝国时代，凡出生在其领地上的人都是英国臣民。

wordForms.noun: subject（话题；学科；受试者；臣民；主语）；subjection（n. 征服，服从）；subjectivity（n. 主观性）
wordForms.verb: subject /səbˈdʒekt/（vt. 使遭受；使服从 —— subjected, subjecting）
wordForms.adjective: subject（受制于…的，主要用于 be subject to 结构；作定语时可表「受统治的」，如 subject peoples）；subjective（主观的）
wordForms.other: 重音「名前动后」：名词/形容词 /ˈsʌbdʒɪkt/，动词 /səbˈdʒekt/（同 record、present、object）。辨析：be subject to sth＝受…支配／易受…影响（to 是介词，后接名词或动名词：subject to inspection / to being inspected）；be subjected to sth＝被施加、被迫经受（多为不好的事），是动词 subject 的被动式，二者不可混用。

classPractice.question: In a country ruled by law, everyone, officials included, is subject ______ the same rules.
classPractice.note: be subject to sth「受…约束／支配」是固定搭配，to 为介词，后接名词；不可写成 subject with/for。

classPractice.question: 任何嫌疑人都不得遭受不公正的对待。（subject）
classPractice.answer: No suspect should be subjected to unfair treatment.
classPractice.note: 「遭受」用被动 be subjected to sth（动词 subject 重音在后 /səbˈdʒekt/）；若写成 be subject to 则变成「受…支配」，意思不对。

translation: vi. 起源，发源，产生（常与 in/from/with 连用）；（交通工具）始发于　vt. 创始，首创，发明
sub_section: 补充词汇（课件重点·非词汇表）
definitionEn: to happen or appear for the first time in a particular place, time or situation; (transitive) to create or start sth new such as an idea, a design or a plan

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 创始，首创，发明（此时为及物动词，宾语是被创造出来的事物）
uncommonMeanings.example: She originated a scheme to protect young inventors' designs.｜她首创了一套保护年轻发明者设计的方案。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【交通】（航班、列车等）始发于某地
uncommonMeanings.example: The flight originating in Shanghai was delayed by fog.｜由上海始发的航班因大雾延误。

posExamples.sentence: Many modern patent rules originated in nineteenth-century Britain.｜许多现代专利规则起源于19世纪的英国。
Her doubts about the contract originated from one unclear clause.｜她对这份合同的怀疑源于其中一个含糊的条款。
It was printers, not writers, who originated the earliest form of copyright.｜最早形式的版权是印刷商而非作家首创的。

collocations.example: Common law originated in medieval England.｜普通法起源于中世纪的英格兰。
Most copyright cases originate from careless copying online.｜多数版权案件源于网上的随意复制。

collocations.translation: 由某人首创，出自某人之手
collocations.example: The proposal to shorten patent terms originated with a student.｜缩短专利期限的提议出自一名学生。
The word 'patent' originated as a term for an open official letter.｜patent 一词最初指一种公开的官方文书。

collocations.phrase: be believed / thought to have originated
collocations.translation: 据信起源于…（谈过去的起源须用不定式完成式）
collocations.example: Trial by jury is thought to have originated in Norman England.｜陪审团审判据信起源于诺曼时期的英格兰。

collocations.phrase: originate an idea / a design / a scheme
collocations.translation: 首创某种想法／设计／方案（及物用法）
collocations.example: He originated a design that later won a national patent.｜他首创的一项设计后来获得了国家专利。

collocations.translation: 原产于某国的商品（贸易与海关用语）
collocations.example: Only goods originating in that region carry the special mark.｜只有原产于该地区的商品才带有此专用标志。

wordForms.noun: origin（起源，出身，常用复数 origins）；originator（创始人，首创者）；originality（独创性，是作品受版权保护的前提）
wordForms.verb: originate（起源；首创 —— originated, originating）
wordForms.adjective: original（最初的；原创的，未被抄袭的）
wordForms.other: 构词：origin + -ate（名词→动词），重音落在第二音节 /əˈrɪdʒɪneɪt/。用法关键：表「起源」时是不及物动词，绝不能用被动——×The idea was originated in Venice. √The idea originated in Venice.；只有表「首创、发明」时才及物（originate a design）。介词分工：originate in（地点／时代）、originate from（原因／来源）、originate with sb（由某人首创）。

classPractice.question: The idea of protecting inventions by law ______ (originate) in Venice, where the first patent statute was passed in 1474.
classPractice.note: 1474 表明是过去的事实，用一般过去时；originate 表「起源」是不及物动词，不能写成 was originated。

classPractice.question: 这场商标纠纷起源于一个简单的误会。The trademark dispute ______ ______ a simple misunderstanding.（用 originate）
classPractice.note: originate from sth 表「源于（某原因）」；叙述过去发生的事用过去式，且不用被动语态。

translation: n. （精密的）仪器，器械；乐器（＝musical instrument）；（达到目的的）手段，工具；【法律】正式文件，法律文书；（飞机等的）仪表
sub_section: 补充词汇（课件重点·非词汇表）
definitionEn: a tool or device used for careful, scientific or delicate work; an object used for producing music; a means by which sth is achieved; (law) a formal written document such as a contract or a patent

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【法律】正式文件，法律文书（如合同、条约、专利证书）
uncommonMeanings.example: A patent is a legal instrument that must be registered.｜专利是一份必须注册的法律文书。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （被用来达到某种目的的）手段，工具，也可指「被人利用的人」
uncommonMeanings.example: He became a mere instrument in his boss's plan.｜他沦为老板计划中的一个工具。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【航空】（飞机、汽车的）仪表；fly on instruments 指依靠仪表飞行
uncommonMeanings.example: The pilot flew on instruments through the thick fog.｜飞行员在浓雾中依靠仪表飞行。

posExamples.sentence: Scientists calibrate each instrument before recording any data.｜科学家在记录数据前会校准每一台仪器。
Law is the chief instrument by which a society keeps order.｜法律是社会维持秩序的主要手段。
The two countries exchanged the instruments of ratification last week.｜两国上周交换了批准书。

collocations.translation: 法律文书（合同、专利、条约等）
collocations.example: A signed contract is a legal instrument binding both sides.｜签署的合同是对双方都有约束力的法律文书。
Education is a powerful instrument of social change.｜教育是推动社会变革的有力工具。

collocations.translation: （喻）粗糙生硬的手段；（字面）钝器
collocations.example: Criminal law is a blunt instrument for stopping online piracy.｜用刑法制止网络盗版是一种生硬的手段。
Precision instruments can reveal the tiniest flaw in a fake.｜精密仪器能查出赝品上最细微的破绽。

collocations.phrase: a musical instrument; play an instrument
collocations.example: She plays three musical instruments and composes her own songs.｜她会演奏三种乐器，还自己作曲。
A red light on the instrument panel warned of engine trouble.｜仪表盘上的红灯提示发动机故障。

collocations.translation: 在…中发挥重要作用（形容词形式的固定考点）
collocations.example: Her research was instrumental in tightening the copyright rules.｜她的研究对收紧版权规则起了重要作用。

wordForms.noun: instrument（仪器；乐器；手段；法律文书）；instrumentation（器械配备；乐器配置）；instrumentalist（器乐演奏者）
wordForms.verb: instrument（vt. 给…装配仪表，仅限工程技术语境，中学不作要求 —— instrumented, instrumenting）
wordForms.adjective: instrumental（起重要作用的；用乐器演奏的）
wordForms.adverb: instrumentally（少用；表「起重要作用」一般用 be instrumental in doing sth，不用副词）
wordForms.other: 词根 stru-「建造、装配」，与 construct、structure、instruct 同源。高频考点：be instrumental in doing sth「在…中起关键作用」，in 为介词，后必须接动名词。辨析：instrument 多指精密仪器或专业器械（surgical/scientific instruments）；tool 指手工工具；device 指有具体功能的装置；乐器只说 musical instrument，不说 music tool。

classPractice.question: 他在起草这部知识产权法的过程中发挥了重要作用。He ______ ______ ______ drafting the intellectual property law.（用 instrument 的形容词形式）
classPractice.note: be instrumental in doing sth 是固定结构：in 为介词，后接动名词 drafting；不可写成 was instrumental to draft。

classPractice.question: 法律应当成为伸张正义的工具，而不是压迫的手段。（instrument）
classPractice.answer: The law should be an instrument of justice, not of oppression.
classPractice.note: an instrument of sth 表「…的工具／手段」；后半句为避免重复，用 not of oppression 承前省略 an instrument。

translation: n. 核心，要点，最重要的部分；（水果的）果核；（地球的）地核；（反应堆的）堆芯　adj. 核心的，最主要的（一般只作定语）　vt. 挖去（水果的）核
sub_section: 补充词汇（课件重点·非词汇表）
definitionEn: the most important or central part of sth; the hard central part of a fruit that contains the seeds; (adj.) most important or essential; (v.) to remove the core from a fruit

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 挖去（苹果、梨等的）果核
uncommonMeanings.example: Peel and core the apples before you bake them.｜烤苹果之前先削皮去核。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【地质／核能】地核；（核反应堆的）堆芯
uncommonMeanings.example: Temperatures at the earth's core exceed 5,000°C.｜地核温度超过5000摄氏度。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【计算机】（处理器的）核心，如 a four-core processor 四核处理器
uncommonMeanings.example: This laptop runs on an eight-core processor.｜这台笔记本电脑用的是八核处理器。

posExamples.sentence: Fairness lies at the core of every workable legal system.｜公平处于每一套行之有效的法律制度的核心。
Respect for other people's work is a core value here.｜尊重他人的劳动成果是这里的一项核心价值观。
Core the pears first, then simmer them for ten minutes.｜先把梨去核，再小火煮十分钟。

collocations.example: Trust sits at the core of the relationship between judge and jury.｜信任处于法官与陪审团关系的核心。

collocations.phrase: the core of the problem / argument
collocations.example: The core of the dispute is who really owns the patent.｜争议的核心是这项专利究竟归谁所有。
Honesty and fairness are the core principles of our school.｜诚实与公平是我校的核心原则。
Basic legal knowledge is now part of the core curriculum.｜基础法律知识现已纳入核心课程。
Selling patents is not the company's core business.｜出售专利并不是这家公司的核心业务。
A hard core of repeat offenders is responsible for most of these crimes.｜这类犯罪大多是少数惯犯所为。

collocations.translation: 彻底地，十足地（放在形容词或动词之后）
collocations.example: He is honest to the core, even when nobody is watching.｜他诚实透顶，哪怕无人监督也是如此。
Don't drop the apple core on the pavement—that's littering.｜别把苹果核扔在人行道上，那是乱丢垃圾。

wordForms.noun: core（核心；果核）；hard core（顽固的核心分子；硬核）
wordForms.verb: core（vt. 去核 —— cored, coring）
wordForms.adjective: core（核心的，一般只作定语）；hard-core（作定语时常加连字符，如 hard-core supporters）
wordForms.adverb: —（core 无副词形式；表「彻底地」用短语 to the core）
wordForms.other: core 作形容词一般只作定语，不作表语，也不受程度副词修饰：√a core subject，×This subject is very core。同音／近形词注意区分：core /kɔː/（核心）、corps /kɔː/（军团，ps 不发音）、chore /tʃɔː/（家务杂事）、corn（谷物）。常见近义：the core of ≈ the heart of ≈ the essence of。

classPractice.question: Whether ideas themselves can be owned lies ______ the core of the copyright debate.
classPractice.note: at the core of sth「处于…的核心」为固定搭配（≈ at the heart of），介词用 at，不用 in。

classPractice.question: 这桩侵权丑闻让整个公司深受震动。（to the core）
classPractice.answer: The scandal over infringement shook the whole company to the core.
classPractice.note: to the core 意为「彻底地、深深地」，置于动词或形容词之后作程度状语，属固定短语，core 不加 s。

translation: adj. 独特的，与众不同的，有辨识度的（因某个特征而容易被认出）
sub_section: 补充词汇（课件重点·非词汇表）
definitionEn: having a special quality, style or appearance that makes sth clearly different from others and easy to recognise

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【商标法】具有显著性的（足以区分商品来源，因而可获注册的）
uncommonMeanings.example: A mark must be distinctive before it can be registered.｜商标须具有显著性才能获准注册。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【语言学】区别性的，如 distinctive feature「区别特征」
uncommonMeanings.example: Voicing is a distinctive feature separating /p/ from /b/.｜清浊是区分 /p/ 与 /b/ 的区别特征。

posExamples.sentence: Her handwriting has a distinctive slant that experts recognise at once.｜她的字迹有一种独特的倾斜，专家一眼就能认出。
Holmes noticed the distinctive stains on the assistant's trouser knees.｜福尔摩斯注意到那伙计裤子膝盖上独特的污渍。
A distinctive brand name is far easier to defend in court.｜独特的品牌名在法庭上要好维护得多。

collocations.example: Bright packaging is this product's most distinctive feature.｜鲜艳的包装是这款产品最显著的特征。
The writer's distinctive style makes any copy easy to spot.｜这位作家风格独特，抄袭之作一眼可辨。
A distinctive logo lets customers recognise the brand at a glance.｜有辨识度的标志让顾客一眼就认出这个品牌。

collocations.translation: 极具辨识度的（highly 是最常见的程度修饰语）
collocations.example: Her jewellery designs are highly distinctive and instantly recognisable.｜她的珠宝设计极具辨识度，一眼就能认出。
This tea has a distinctive smoky flavour from the mountains.｜这种茶有山间独特的烟熏味。
The bird has distinctive black markings on both wings.｜这种鸟双翼上有独特的黑色斑纹。
Careful branding gave the small firm a distinctive identity.｜精心的品牌打造赋予这家小公司独特的形象。

wordForms.noun: distinction（区别；卓越，优异，如 graduate with distinction）；distinctiveness（独特性；【商标法】显著性）
wordForms.verb: distinguish（vt. 区分，辨别 —— distinguish A from B / between A and B）
wordForms.adjective: distinctive（有辨识度的）；distinct（清晰的；截然不同的）；distinguished（卓越的，著名的）；distinguishable（可辨别的）
wordForms.adverb: distinctively（以独特的方式）；distinctly（清楚地，明显地）
wordForms.other: 【核心易混】distinctive 强调「有别于他者、易于识别」，修饰 logo、style、smell 等特征；distinct 强调「清晰可辨」或「截然不同」，固定用 be distinct from（×be distinctive from）。副词同理：I distinctly remember signing it.（清楚地记得）≠ distinctively（以独特方式）。构词链：distinguish（v.）→ distinct（adj.）→ distinctive（adj.）；词根 -stinct-/-stingu-「刺、做记号」引申为「区分」，同族词有 instinct、extinguish。

classPractice.question: To be registered, a trademark must be ______ (distinct / distinctive) enough for shoppers to tell one brand from another.
classPractice.note: 此处强调「有辨识度、能与他者区别开」，用 distinctive；distinct 多表「清晰的」或用于 be distinct from「与…截然不同」。

classPractice.question: 这个品牌独特的红色标志已被注册为商标。（distinctive）
classPractice.answer: The brand's distinctive red logo has been registered as a trademark.
classPractice.note: distinctive 作定语修饰 logo；「已被注册」用现在完成时的被动 has been registered，register sth as a trademark 为常用搭配。

translation: adj. 安全的，有保障的；牢固的，固定好的；安心的，无忧的；（工作、地位）稳固的　vt.（尤指经努力）获得，取得；保障，保护，使安全；把…固定牢
sub_section: 补充词汇（课件重点·非词汇表）
definitionEn: (adj.) safe from harm or loss, firmly fixed in position, or free from worry; (v.) to obtain or achieve sth, especially after effort; to make sth safe, or to fasten it firmly

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （经过努力）获得，取得，谋得（正式，≈ obtain 但强调「争取到」）
uncommonMeanings.example: After long negotiations, she secured a contract with a major publisher.｜经过长时间谈判，她与一家大出版社签下了合同。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 把…拴牢，固定好（使不松动、不脱落）
uncommonMeanings.example: He secured the cellar door with a heavy iron bar.｜他用一根粗铁棍把地下室的门闩牢了。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【金融】以（财产）作担保／抵押（常用 be secured on/against sth）
uncommonMeanings.example: The loan was secured against their family house.｜这笔贷款以他们的家宅作抵押。

posExamples.sentence: The company secured exclusive rights to the new formula.｜公司取得了该新配方的独家权利。
Keep your passwords secure so that hackers cannot steal your designs.｜保管好密码，让黑客偷不走你的设计。
With the patent granted, her position in the market felt secure.｜专利获批后，她在市场上的地位显得稳固了。

collocations.example: The firm secured the trademark for its new logo within six months.｜这家公司在半年内为新标志取得了商标。
A written contract secures fair payment for every author.｜书面合同为每位作者争取到了公平的报酬。

collocations.phrase: secure a job / a place / a loan
collocations.example: She secured a place at law school after three interviews.｜经过三轮面试，她拿到了法学院的入学名额。
No online file is completely secure from determined hackers.｜面对铁了心的黑客，没有哪个在线文件是绝对安全的。
Employees feel secure when their contracts are clearly written.｜合同写得清楚，员工才会感到安心。

collocations.phrase: a secure connection / a secure server
collocations.example: Always upload your designs through a secure connection.｜上传设计稿务必使用安全连接。
A single successful patent made the inventor financially secure.｜一项成功的专利让这位发明家经济上有了保障。

wordForms.noun: security（安全；保安；担保物；复数 securities 指「证券」）；insecurity（不安全；不安全感）
wordForms.verb: secure（vt. 获得；保障；固定 —— secured, securing）
wordForms.adjective: secure（安全的，牢固的）；insecure（不安全的；缺乏自信的）；secured（有担保的，如 a secured loan）
wordForms.adverb: securely（牢固地，安全地）；insecurely（不牢固地）
wordForms.other: 词源 se-「没有」+ cura「忧虑」→「无忧的」，故有「安心的」一义（同根 cure, curious）。动词的「获得」义是高考高频考点，语域较正式：secure a patent/contract/job ≈ obtain，但突出「费力争取到」。介词搭配：be secure against / from sth（免受…侵害），不用 to；secure sth for sb（为某人争取到某物）。

classPractice.question: After years of testing and paperwork, the team finally ______ (secure) a patent for their design.
classPractice.note: After years of... 与 finally 提示动作已完成，用一般过去时；secure 在此为及物动词，意为「（经努力）获得」。

classPractice.question: 只有当你的文件被妥善保护时，你的创意才能免受剽窃。Only when your files are kept ______ can your ideas be safe from theft.（用 secure）
classPractice.note: keep + 宾语 + 形容词，故填形容词 secure「安全的、有保障的」；Only when 从句置于句首时主句用部分倒装 can your ideas be...。

partOfSpeech: vi.（不及物动词：无被动语态，一般不用进行时；另有极罕见的铁路名词用法 n. /ˈkɒnsɪst/，高考不考）
translation: vi. 由…组成，由…构成（consist of）；在于，本质是（consist in）；（正式、偏旧）与…一致，相符（consist with）
sub_section: 补充词汇（课件重点·非词汇表）
definitionEn: to be formed or made up of particular parts, things or people (consist of); to have sth as its main or essential feature (consist in). Consist is intransitive: it has no passive form and is not normally used in the progressive.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （正式、偏旧）consist with sth：与…一致，与…相符（现代英语更常说 be consistent with）
uncommonMeanings.example: The witness's story does not consist with the facts we have gathered.｜证人的说法与我们掌握的事实并不相符。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （美国铁路行业术语，读音重音前移 /ˈkɒnsɪst/）列车编组：一列火车所挂车厢与机车的组合
uncommonMeanings.example: The freight train's consist included forty grain cars.｜这列货车的编组里有四十节运粮车厢。

posExamples.sentence: A healthy lifestyle consists of regular exercise, balanced meals and enough sleep.｜健康的生活方式由规律运动、均衡饮食和充足睡眠组成。
For me, the fun of hiking consists in the talk along the way, not in reaching the top.｜对我来说，徒步的乐趣在于一路上的交谈，而不在于登顶。

posExamples.partOfSpeech: vi.（consisting of 作后置定语，= which consists of）
posExamples.sentence: We watched a documentary consisting of five short films about ocean life.｜我们看了一部由五个海洋生物短片组成的纪录片。

collocations.translation: 由…组成，由…构成（整体→部分；绝不用被动）
collocations.example: A balanced breakfast consists of milk, eggs and whole-grain bread.｜均衡的早餐由牛奶、鸡蛋和全麦面包组成。

collocations.phrase: consist in sth / in doing sth
collocations.example: True friendship consists in standing by someone when things go wrong.｜真正的友谊在于对方遇到麻烦时依然守在他身边。
The audience consisted mainly of parents and younger students.｜观众主要由家长和低年级学生组成。
This year's paper consists entirely of reading and writing tasks.｜今年的试卷完全由阅读和写作任务组成。

collocations.translation: 只不过由…构成，充其量不过是…
collocations.example: His so-called apology consisted of little more than a shrug.｜他所谓的道歉只不过是耸了耸肩罢了。

collocations.translation: …由哪些部分组成？（疑问句式，仍不可用被动）
collocations.example: What exactly does the training course consist of?｜这门培训课程具体由哪些内容组成？

collocations.phrase: consisting of ...（现在分词短语作后置定语）
collocations.example: A team consisting of three students from our class won the debate.｜一支由我们班三名同学组成的队伍赢得了辩论赛。

wordForms.noun: consistency（一致性；连贯性；（液体的）稠度）；consistence（同义，罕用）。注意：表示“构成、成分”要用 composition / make-up，不能用 consistency。
wordForms.verb: consist（consists / consisted / consisted / consisting，规则变化）；同义表达：comprise（vt.）、be composed of、be made up of
wordForms.adjective: consistent（一致的；始终如一的），be consistent with sth 与…相符；反义 inconsistent（前后矛盾的）
wordForms.other: 词源：con-（共同）+ sistere（站立）→“站在一起”→由…组成。三大高频错点：①不及物动词，无被动，×be consisted of，要么 consist of，要么 be made up of / be composed of；②一般不用进行时，×is consisting of；③consist of（列出组成部分）≠ consist in（指出本质、关键所在）。与 comprise 对比：comprise 是及物动词，The team comprises eleven players.；口语中常见的 be comprised of 有争议，考试用 be made up of / be composed of 更稳妥。主谓一致取决于主语本身：Our team consists of...（单数）／The materials consist of...（复数）。

classPractice.question: Our school choir ______ (consist) of forty students from three different grades.
classPractice.note: consist 是不及物动词，绝不能写 is consisted of；主语 Our school choir 视为整体作单数，故用 consists；该词也不用进行时（×is consisting of）。

classPractice.question: 用 in / of 填空：①The training course consists ______ four modules and a final project. ②The charm of the old town consists ______ its narrow stone streets and slow pace.
classPractice.note: consist of 列举“由哪些部分组成”；consist in 指出“本质／魅力／关键在于”。②句强调古镇魅力之所在，故用 in。

classPractice.question: Our volunteer group is consisted of twelve high school students.
classPractice.answer: is consisted of → consists of（或把 consist 换掉：is made up of / is composed of）
classPractice.note: consist 无被动语态，这是该词最常见的错误；若一定要用被动结构表达“由…组成”，须换成 be made up of / be composed of。
